# Verdant Engine

> Universal 3D browser and WebAssembly game engine in Rust (`crates/verdant-core`) mechanized with Prism, exact `uor-matmul` tensor contractions, progressive `UORC` multi-LOD streaming, archetype ECS, SAH BVH culling, procedural geometry, skeletal animation, PBR materials, portable W3C WGSL shader validation, Khronos glTF 2.0 binary export, 60Hz rigid-body and GJK physics, NavMesh pathfinding, Woodworth spatial audio, and SHA-256 world snapshots.

## Documentation

- [Verdant Engine documentation](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/): Build fast 3D games and interactive worlds for the web and Rust.
- [Build your first 3D world](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/getting-started/): Create a Rust 3D scene, step rigid-body physics, and export a binary asset.
- [Author terrain, shaders, and spatial audio](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/guides/custom-game-world/): Build 3D terrain meshes, check portable shaders, and mix 3D sound.
- [Stream high-resolution scenes with UORC](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/guides/progressive-uorc-streaming/): Stream multi-LOD 3D scenes smoothly up to lossless source detail.
- [Verdant Core API reference](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/reference/engine-api/): Look up engine modules, core types, CLI commands, and 60fps budgets.
- [Portable tensor kernels and UORC streaming](https://afflom.github.io/verdant-engine/docs/explanation/tensor-and-uorc-streaming/): Learn how exact tensor contractions and UORC chains run in every browser.
